A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All pages, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including Appendices A–E in v1 and A–F in v2.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and the appendices report original attack-success, transferability, mitigation and sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: Original classification experiments remain, with additional typographic-attack comparisons and Flickr30K retrieval results.

M1.justification: The retrieval, OCR categorization, artifact selection and placement procedures remain unchanged. Description-based mitigation is retained: captioning was already described in v1's introduction and Appendix E. The rewritten Section 5 does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: New Appendix F evaluates image-to-text retrieval on Flickr30K, substantially extending task coverage beyond classification. CC12M artifact mining and the five classification tasks using FairFace, CelebA, FGVC Aircraft and Country211 are retained.

E2.justification: v2 introduces the first direct empirical comparisons against prior typographic attacks, covering attack success in Figure 5 and response to artifact-aware prompting in Figure 10. v1 discusses this prior attack family but does not include it in the corresponding reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the stated estimation sample from 10 to 32 images per class. Figure 4(b) adds a separate LAION-2B condition, Appendix F introduces Top-1 retrieval evaluation, and mitigation is reported through relative success-rate reduction. The masking-validated classification protocol remains; these revisions do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The pretraining-curation analysis gains a separate LAION-2B condition, and the mitigation analysis now examines effectiveness relative to typographic attacks. Existing placement, sample-size, size/transparency, artifact-combination and transferability analyses remain, with some numerical revisions.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 9 reports error bars for both mitigation prompting conditions; its replacement, v2 Figure 10, reports relative reductions without uncertainty. Error bars and shaded bands remain elsewhere. No repeated-run counts, seeds or statistical-test procedures are added.

E6.justification: v2 adds typographic-comparison results and retrieval success rates of 83.4%, 63.8% and 63.4% for graphics with text, graphics without text and text, respectively. Existing results also change: top-center placement for graphics without text changes from 37% in v1 Figure 11 to 38.19% in v2 Figure 12. Model and dataset plots are revised, and absolute mitigation rates are replaced by relative reductions. Changed settings preclude treating these as demonstrated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The attack formulation, opposing-class subset, artifact-impact score, complexity argument and masking-validated ASR definition are mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: attacks beyond class-matching text, efficient artifact search, transferability, combined attacks approaching 100% success and incomplete mitigation. New comparisons support these claims without substantively redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 removes the specific binary-loss explanation for SigLIP's robustness and acknowledges its different pretraining data. It adds interpretations that optimizing beyond class-matching text improves attack effectiveness and that prompting defenses work less well against these attacks than against typographic attacks. Appendix F extends applicability to retrieval.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, names EasyOCR and documents fixed pretraining/architecture controls for model comparisons. These are disclosures rather than established setting changes. Section 5 adds overhead information but omits the earlier explicit OCR/logo-detector description; several captions also drop their statements about averaging across models and datasets.

R1.justification: EasyOCR and Flickr30K Entities references are added. The related-work framework remains substantially unchanged, while Sections 4–5 sharpen empirical positioning against the already-cited typographic attacks.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes the name Web Artifact Attacks, edits signposting and captions, rewrites the mitigation discussion, and adds acknowledgments and Appendix F. The main section order and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Result displays are substantially reworked: v2 adds a baseline-comparison figure, replaces the mitigation chart, rotates the confidence boxplots, revises axes and legends across several plots, and rearranges the caption examples. The pipeline and artifact-example figures are relocated; much appendix content is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Direct typographic-attack comparisons address v1's lack of empirical context against its principal predecessor, while code, OCR and comparison-control disclosures improve reproducibility. Retrieval results broaden the evidence, but Appendix F provides little protocol detail. Replacing the mitigation plot also removes absolute rates and uncertainty. The additions therefore provide a limited net improvement rather than a substantial overall advance.
